start_here: Say to your AI: "I added the DNS records, so ask Resend to check domain 4dd369bc-aa82-4ff3-97de-514ae3000ee0 again." It runs tool:check-an-email-sending-domain.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it asks your email-sending account to look at one domain's DNS again and writes nothing of its own.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once so your key is held under the name resend-api-key; the key is never typed into the request.
2. Add the DNS records tool:add-an-email-sending-domain gave you, at your DNS host, and wait a few minutes.
3. Say to your AI: "Check my Resend domain <id> again". It calls tools:run with tool tool:check-an-email-sending-domain and {"domain_id": "<id>"}.
4. The check runs on Resend's side; the answer only confirms the request. Read the result with tool:read-an-email-sending-domain.

worked_examples.title: Ask Resend to verify example.com again
worked_examples.ask: Ask Resend to check domain 4dd369bc-aa82-4ff3-97de-514ae3000ee0 again.
worked_examples.given: From test/list-email-sending-domains.test.mjs (the id shape) and tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: the row POSTs https://api.resend.com/domains/4dd369bc-aa82-4ff3-97de-514ae3000ee0/verify with no body and returns Resend's reply unchanged; its output_schema names only id.
worked_examples.hands_back: {"id":"4dd369bc-aa82-4ff3-97de-514ae3000ee0"}, then tool:read-an-email-sending-domain shows the new status.
